summary: Delivered the PH-291 cross-domain read-only operations reconciliation overview in the delivery layer. The new `pmo_plugins/delivery/operations_read_services.py` exposes `ops_reconciliation_overview(member, *, as_of=None, period=None)` which aggregates already-delivered owner facts into six sections: contracts (pending changes / terminated contracts / approved lines still active under terminated contracts), settlement (active open items, over-cleared items, refunds, bank returns, refunds without matching clearance, derived remaining balance), management revenue (posted recognitions, reversed recognitions, terminated-still-recognized, recognized vs active-settled net difference), time (pending/confirmed billable confirmations, confirmed minutes, unapproved timesheets), onboarding (PH-274 preview is stateless, so counts/totals are null plus the `import_preview_persistence_not_implemented` missing code instead of 0) and cash (posted transactions, missing classifications, posted in/out/net; for pm the cash section is null plus `cash_not_scoped_to_project`). Role matrix: owner/finance/auditor full, pm limited to managed/visible projects, member denied; history reads survive module disable because the new `modules/delivery/ops-reconciliation-overview/` route is declared `history_read` (appended to an in-memory metadata copy in delivery/urls.py since domain_metadata.py is outside the exact whitelist, so no gate weakening). Everything is deliberately read-only: no writes, no audit, no receipts, no session persistence, no migration, no second insights owner. Tests assert derived (not echoed) values, null-plus-missing semantics, ref cap/truncation, period and as_of filtering, role/scope isolation, invalid-input rejections, module-disabled history, and zero INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE SQL plus unchanged fact/audit/event counts. View/form/template/URL wiring and 15 scoped tests are included; no contract schema or business write path was changed.

review.reviewer: independent PH-291 cross-domain-operations-overview reviewer (fresh context, read-only)
findings: BLOCKER 1 - route metadata is declared in a parallel copy inside delivery/urls.py, not in the plugin's canonical domain_metadata: `DELIVERY_METADATA = {**DOMAIN_METADATA, 'routes': [*DOMAIN_METADATA['routes'], {'name':'ops_reconciliation_overview', ..., 'access':'history_read'}]}` is passed to the SDK only from this module. PH-291's allowed_paths intentionally do not include `pmo_plugins/delivery/domain_metadata.py`, so the worker created a second metadata source instead of extending the canonical one. Even though the resulting route is registered through prepare_plugin_entry_point, this bypasses the single domain-metadata contract that the plugin SDK/governance expects and can drift or evade future metadata/gating checks. Fix: add `pmo_plugins/delivery/domain_metadata.py` to the planning whitelist and declare the route there (leaving urls.py to import the canonical metadata), then assert the route is present in DOMAIN_METADATA; do not ship a parallel metadata copy.

BLOCKER 2 - pm scope leaks company-wide settlement refunds/returns and is inconsistent with the null+missing cash rule: `_settlement_section` filters OpenItems by visible projects but queries `Refund`/`BankReturn` only by organization and computes `refund_total`, `return_total`, `refunds_without_clearance`, and refunded/cleared cash-id sets org-wide for every role, including pm. A pm therefore sees financial totals from projects managed by other users even though `_cash_section` correctly returns null+`cash_not_scoped_to_project` for pm. Fix: for pm either return null+missing for cash-linked refund/return coverage (no project attribution) or scope to the managed projects' OpenItems/Settlements, and add a pm regression with a refund in a non-managed project.

BLOCKER 3 - pm time section compares integer contract-line pks with the UUIDField BillableConfirmation.contract_line_id: `line_ids = ContractLine.objects...values_list('pk')` (ints) then `confirmations.filter(contract_line_id__in=list(line_ids))`. PH-269 stores `contract_line_id` as a UUID5 (UUIDField), so SQLite can silently return no matches and PostgreSQL can reject the integer comparison; the fixture's `BillableConfirmation(... contract_line_id=self.approved_line.pk)` masks this by inserting an integer into a UUID field in tests. Fix: derive/select the UUID5 keys consistently (the same derivation used by the time owner) or scope by canonical contract-line refs, and add a pm time-count regression using a real UUID5 confirmation.

PASSED CHECKS: read-only purity is otherwise verified (CaptureQueriesContext has no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and fact/audit/event counts unchanged); six sections; settlement remaining=gross-active cleared (20000 in the gold case) not the input amount; revenue difference=recognized-settled; cash net=in-out; time minutes is a separate unit/field; onboarding null+`import_preview_persistence_not_implemented`; pm cash null+`cash_not_scoped_to_project`; integer cents and refs<=50; period is an optional read-only filter (Lead-authorized deviation from the original as_of-only signature) and is accepted; no migration/vendor-specific assertion/verify_integrity change; 13 changed files all in PH-291 allowed_paths; task in_review, manifest=PH-291. EVIDENCE: check ok=true/216; manage.py check exit0; makemigrations clean; scoped 15 OK; full suite 1001/5F+3E/69 (known 8 macOS baseline only); verify_integrity fresh DB ok; verify-change --base fa1ca8d --task PH-291 only review/acceptance gates, no path_out_of_scope.

deviations: Route wiring: the frozen PH-291 whitelist does not include `pmo_plugins/delivery/domain_metadata.py`, but the SDK requires a declared route for access/dispatch. I appended the `ops_reconciliation_overview` route (`history_read`) to an in-memory copy of DOMAIN_METADATA inside `pmo_plugins/delivery/urls.py` (whitelisted) and bound the handler there; domain_metadata.py and all other files stayed untouched. This keeps the read-only/history semantics without expanding the read/write gate.

The spec's frozen service signature is `ops_reconciliation_overview(member, *, as_of=None)`; per the Lead's explicit requirement I added an optional `period` (YYYY-MM) filter to the service and page. It is additive, read-only and covered by validation/tests; no existing interface was changed.

Onboarding preview section: PH-274's preview is deliberately stateless at this BASE and PH-289 (persistence) is still proposed, so the section reports counts/totals as null plus `import_preview_persistence_not_implemented` rather than fabricating zero; pm cash is likewise null plus `cash_not_scoped_to_project` because cash facts have no project FK.

No audit is written (spec allowed an optional generic audit; the Lead required zero audit), no receipt/session persistence is used, and no migration or contract-schema change was made. The module-disabled page relies on the new history_read route instead of weakening enablement checks.
Refs are capped at 50 per section with an explicit `truncated` flag; the cap is tested with 55 pending changes (refs length 50, truncated true).
